answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to costly, verifiable work: each agent locks a small stake and earns reputation only through attested jobs recorded in a shared grove of peer endorsements, so one operator spinning up thousands of clones gains nothing — the clones share a single ferrous-hard budget and no history. Newcomers start with narrow permissions and must survive a probationary gale of small, independently verified tasks before touching valuable work, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents compound trust.
